necessary_context.content: psi(x)=g(x)+sup_y[f(x,y)-r(y)], X=dom(g), Y=dom(r). Primal space is Euclidean R^p; dual space R^q has norm ||.|| and dual norm ||.||_*. f is continuous; g,r are proper closed functions. d_y is a distance-generating function, convex on Y and continuously differentiable and 1-strongly convex on Y^o={y in Y: partial d_y(y) nonempty}. V_y(y,y')=d_y(y)-d_y(y')-<grad d_y(y'),y-y'> for y' in Y^o.
necessary_context.name: Problem and geometry

necessary_context.content: f(.,y) is rho-weakly convex for every y in Y; f(x,.) is concave for every x in X; r is closed and mu-strongly convex relative to V_y, mu>=0; g is closed convex; psi*=min_x psi(x)>-infinity. Section 3 uses gamma>0 with 1/gamma>rho for Moreau differentiation.
necessary_context.name: Assumption 1

necessary_context.content: For each (x,y) in X times Y the stochastic vectors satisfy (E g_x,-E g_y) in partial_x f times partial_y[-f], E||g_x||_2^2<=M_x^2 and E||g_y||_*^2<=M_y^2 for M_x,M_y>0. Q_g=max_X g-min_X g and Q_r=max_Y r-min_Y r are finite. D1 sets mu=0, D_x=max_{x,x' in X}||x-x'||_2 finite and D_y=sqrt(2 max_Y d_y-2 min_Y d_y) finite.
necessary_context.name: Assumption 2 D1
